decisions.statement: serverless workloads scale to zero when idle
every pull request names what it deletes
every GitHub artifact, code comment and document is written in English
before 1.0, a feature that breaks nothing ships in a patch, and only a breaking change makes a minor
with a support catalog, only a commit that touches a project the catalog lists as stable, or an unlisted project a stable one depends on, advances its version line past a patch
the core CLI declares no development verb: build, test, lint, serve, run, format, package, publish, deploy, generate and validate come from @putnami/dev, which the language extensions depend on
there is no kit or profile concept: installing an extension installs its extensionDependencies, and that graph decides what a workspace gets
putnami init --extension <language> installs that language extension, and its dependencies bring the rest
anonymous usage telemetry stays in the core CLI
the core CLI computes a tree's version before any cache key; the version get|tag and changelog commands belong to @putnami/dev
@putnami/contributor ships a compiled executable and owns change verify|finalize|language
@putnami/dev does not depend on @putnami/contributor, which installs only on explicit request: a workspace receives the contributor skills and agents only when someone asks for @putnami/contributor
putnami migrate agent-content is deleted in the next minor release, with no transition window
an extension command calls the collaboration providers through an RPC call to the core, made with an SDK client
the planner and the scheduler are packages, and import paths set the engine boundary: only internal/engine names planner.Plan and scheduler.RunPlan
the change noun carries the change workflow: change verify, change finalize and change language replace tree verify, proposals finalize and contributor language
sessions export and sessions summary stay in the core, because they read the host's session store
@putnami/dev owns the version noun; version list|use, which list and switch the installed CLI binaries, become cli list|use
contributor machine-load becomes doctor --machine, in the core
the core's dev noun is deleted: dev extension validate becomes extensions validate <path>, and dev template <action> becomes templates validate|test|package <path>
an extension manifest declares the kind of each command it adds, in an additive contract rung that ships with the traits that replace verb-name checks
a feature declaration may list the commands and MCP tools that carry the feature

Cloud deletes its nine alias subcommands (tokens, distribution, oci, publish-archives, track, report, validate-config, publish-config, publish-migration) in a dedicated Cloud pull request that ships as a breaking Cloud release

publication uploads have two uploaders: a standard one in @putnami/dev that uses the standard protocols (OCI, npm), and one in @putnami/cloud for the Putnami registries, which can optimize transfer and cost
